component_spec_check.method: Instantiated both modes in an isolated copy and registered each in native Registry without compiling a graph.

conclusion: The frozen successor has a sound source-bound affine poll-factor implementation for the selected six-row block and retains both original modes. The independently reproduced tiny logp/gradient tests, 4000-row bank equality, exact coefficient recomputation, strict symmetry checks, token ownership, and component-source identity support the supplied-state claim. It is not evidence that the actual full graph builds or is normalized/qualified.

findings.evidence: Both original modes remain supported. The scalar mapping is extracted from the exact pinned native `Measurement.observations` AST prefix (candidate lookup, first/second IDs, and log-rate difference), and selection requires six rows in the authenticated order with direction exactly all ones and zero offset. The incumbent branch uses the exact original fixed covariance; the actual branch loads the pinned 4000-row covariance/weight bank and pinned scalar coefficients. Rerun agrees with the original provider logp and all seven-rate gradients at all twelve supplied states. All covariance rows/weights match exactly and recomputed precision/center/base arrays have zero error.

The wrapper pins its selection and all eight selected dependencies; it extracts source-bound native means and validates full Problem/parent plus exact contest_map. It calls unchanged native `Measurement.observations` with only polls emptied, then claims the exact same single factor name and six ordered poll tokens. Supplied tests intercept native delegation and confirm nonpoll data and protected-parent context; a no-graph registry check confirms both modes preserve role/stages/parameter_patterns and that ComponentSpec binds this provider file SHA.
findings.limit: The delegation test checks forwarded context, not evaluated CES/report likelihoods. Full graph ownership, inventory equality and runtime registration into the complete model were not built.

findings.evidence: All comparisons are tiny supplied-rate PyMC graphs over a 7-entry log-rate vector; the native nonpoll delegate is intercepted. There is no complete TX graph, all-parameter point, parent normalization, sample, posterior predictive or forecast. The result appropriately calls this supplied-state-only evidence and states the current-only calibration bank is not prospective evidence.

An initial attempt with the repository `.venv` failed during PyMC import because its installed `arviz` lacked `InferenceData`; rerunning the same copied check in the explicitly pinned calibration-v1 runtime passed. This was an environment mismatch, not a source/test defect.

independent_rerun.method: Copied provider.py, check.py, selection.json and native-mapping-source.txt to a fresh sibling temporary directory; ran only check.py with the pinned calibration-v1 runtime and isolated temporary PyTensor compiledir. Output/cache were removed after inspection. No actual graph code path exists in the check.

review_sha256_note: New review only; Sol’s frozen packet and existing source files were not modified.
scope: Frozen provider/source/result review, bounded supplied-state rerun in fresh copy, and tiny native-registry ComponentSpec check. No actual TX full graph or owner job was built or changed.
